note: Document-first business frontend with direct CV editing, template-Mod import/selection and structured job analysis using native text-generation runners. CV imports use native owner-session CLI threads in the wrapper; existing model and permission defaults remain native. The app backend is rebuilt and pinned separately; installed T3 remains untouched. The shared CV content editor, separate form captions and per-entry PDF-inclusion controls are built, browser-verified and deployed. The frontend build was completed without source maps; native provider and permission behavior remains unchanged. The wrapper's empty Lua-list correction is deployed. The v2 form-Primitives renderer reuses the content editor with configurable labels in the normal CV workspace on the prototype branch. Its separate frontend/server/build commands were removed; the regular candidate app build and browser flow pass. V2 now shares the existing document editor's inline text control and compact document styling, without imposing fixed CV fields. Every entries primitive and legacy CV section uses the same mandatory EntryCollection controls: new entries first, same-section desktop drag/drop, one-step/top/bottom arrows, keyboard ordering, PDF inclusion, confirmed deletion and order-only undo preserving newer edits/additions. This is app-owned behavior, not generated mod UI or an optional manifest feature. Free-form period strings are never silently parsed for date sorting. Built-in CV/Portfolio demos were removed from production sources/catalog and moved to test-only fixtures; unused historical demo packages are deleted, bound old versions and all CV values preserved, and new bindings to retired demo IDs rejected. The v2 form-storage backend and complete upload/prompt/check/publication path are deployed; existing CV content is not automatically converted. New normal imports request the declarative v2 form and adapter, while legacy v1 remains supported. Model-facing guidance includes primitive/binding rules and an actionable same-thread question/recheck flow. Four form-derived PDF scenarios gate immutable imported versions without shadow copies in the business database. The 14-PDF browser proof uses a substituted agent. One subsequently authorized native default-model run generated a schema-valid form for a public Overleaf template; missing NewTX dependencies initially blocked compilation. On explicit user request the same agent continued once to install original checksum-locked CTAN packages in an isolated candidate builder and repair two adapter defects, without host installation or existing Debian package upgrades. The candidate is independently rebuilt, tested and pinned. A small section-spacing repair followed independent visual inspection. The same import now passes all four normal app proof builds and is selectable as a reviewed fixed version; existing CV bindings remain unchanged. New native starts receive BUILD-ENVIRONMENT.json and a contract to install missing original dependencies in an isolated candidate, while production pin activation remains an explicit operator action. Its valid mcp:-namespaced thread ID exposed an overly narrow wrapper check, now fixed with encoded URL segments and a red-to-green regression test. The existing completed test thread was reattached and checked without another model run. This public-template real-agent/PDF proof is complete with documented agent repairs and an independent spacing correction; it is not a general template or model-quality guarantee. Build history supports guarded manual deletion and opt-in, success-only pruning per application/document kind. Finalized and referenced builds remain protected, and a durable cleanup journal survives file-system failures. The new preference is deployed disabled; no production builds were deleted by the rollout. A subsequent client-only PDF preview fix is deployed: business CV/cover previews use the existing native-PDF/PDF.js viewer rather than a separate sandboxed PDF iframe. Actual HTTPS PDF.js text and page pixels were verified on desktop/mobile without service restarts or data changes. Concurrent branding assets are retained. Thread details no longer render workspace/environment selection or version-control controls, including saved visibility overrides and menu/settings choices. The active app uses only its same-origin web server; stored foreign targets are retained but not connected. Browser/recording and peer RPC/MCP handlers, remote followers, desktop activation, native mobile client access and automatic settlement are retired. Legacy data/contracts remain readable. Application and chat views share the overview breadcrumb; Diagnostics UI, workspace defaults and snooze triggers are retired. The legacy chat archive view and extra optional-chat hint are removed. Legacy business chat events and the old Pi session were subsequently purged from active storage on explicit user request, with a consistent backup; current native chats remain unchanged. Full retirement of other previously marked native features remains incomplete.
